items.stem: Describe the study by Deci (1971) and explain what it shows about the undermining effect of extrinsic rewards on intrinsic motivation.
items.answer: Deci (1971). Aim: to investigate the effect of external rewards on intrinsic motivation. Method: 24 university students in the USA solved Soma cube puzzles in three one-hour sessions; in session 2 the experimental group was paid $1 for each puzzle solved. In each session the experimenter left the room for 8 minutes and recorded how long participants spent on the puzzles when free to do anything. Findings: paid participants spent less free-choice time on the puzzles in session 3 than in session 1, whereas unpaid controls slightly increased their time Link: the undermining effect of extrinsic rewards on intrinsic motivation.
items.markingKey: Up to 2 marks for accurate description of the study (aim, method, findings: paid participants spent less free-choice time on the puzzles in session 3 than in session 1, whereas unpaid controls slightly increased their time); up to 2 marks for explicitly linking the findings to the undermining effect of extrinsic rewards on intrinsic motivation. items.stem: With reference to Lepper, Greene and Nisbett (1973), explain how research has investigated the overjustification effect.

Method: Nursery school children in California who already liked drawing with felt-tip markers drew under one of three conditions: expected award (a "Good Player" certificate), unexpected award or no award. items.stem: "Self-determination theory provides a convincing explanation of human motivation." To what extent is this view justified?
items.answer: SDT is well supported and widely applied, but its universality and measurement need further testing.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: Deci (1971) and Lepper et al. (1973): undermining effect; Deci et al. (1999) meta-analysis of 128 studies; Williams et al. (1996): autonomous motivation predicts weight loss; applied successfully in education, health and work. Arguments against: much evidence is self-report and correlational; cultural debate - is autonomy valued equally in collectivist cultures? (Iyengar and Lepper, 1999); needs are hard to measure directly; reward effects are smaller in real settings (Cameron and Pierce, 1994). items.stem: With reference to Schultz, Dayan and Montague (1997), explain how research has investigated the reward prediction error role of dopamine.
items.answer: Schultz, Dayan and Montague (1997). Aim: to explain the firing of midbrain dopamine neurons during reward learning in terms of a prediction-error signal. items.stem: With reference to Knutson et al. (2001), explain how research has investigated the role of the nucleus accumbens in reward anticipation.
items.answer: Knutson et al. (2001). Aim: to investigate whether anticipation of increasing monetary rewards activates the nucleus accumbens. items.stem: In a study of volunteers in Cape Town, both groups worked on a jigsaw puzzle in session 1. In session 2 the reward group was paid 20 rand per completed section; the control group received nothing. In sessions 1 and 3, free-choice time on the task was recorded. Reward group: mean 236 seconds (session 1), 167 seconds (session 3). Control group: mean 246 seconds (session 1), 281 seconds (session 3). Calculate the change in mean free-choice time for each group and state what the results suggest.
items.answer: Reward group change = 167 - 236 = -69 seconds; control change = 281 - 246 = +35 seconds. The reward appears to have reduced intrinsic motivation (overjustification).
items.markingKey: A1 reward change -69. A1 control change +35. R1 reward group decreased relative to control - consistent with the undermining effect.

items.stem: Describe the study by Warneken and Tomasello (2008) and explain what it shows about intrinsic prosocial motivation and the undermining effect.
items.answer: Warneken and Tomasello (2008). Aim: to investigate whether extrinsic rewards undermine young children's helping. Method: 36 20-month-old children in Leipzig had many opportunities to help an adult (e.g. retrieving an out-of-reach object); in the treatment phase they received a toy reward, praise or nothing for helping; a test phase followed with no rewards. Findings: children who had received a material reward helped less often in the test phase than children who had been praised or received nothing Link: intrinsic prosocial motivation and the undermining effect.

items.stem: With reference to Olds and Milner (1954), explain how research has investigated biological reward systems in the brain.

items.stem: Using Prochaska and DiClemente (1983) as supporting evidence, explain the transtheoretical model of health behaviour change.
items.answer: Prochaska and DiClemente (1983). Aim: to investigate whether smokers use different processes of change at different stages. items.stem: Critically assess the view that motivation can be explained by dopamine activity in the brain. Consider at least one methodological and one ethical or cultural issue.
